caption:
Write this in a machine coding round and the Network tab fills up while the interviewer watches.

Look at the card. filters is created again on every render. It has the same values, but it's a new object, and React compares dependencies with Object.is, which checks the reference.

New object, so the effect runs. If fetchList sets state, that causes a render, which creates a new object, which runs the effect again.

The fix: depend on the primitive values the effect actually uses. Build the object inside the effect.

If you need the object outside too, useMemo can keep the same reference between renders.

Source: react.dev, Removing Effect Dependencies.
